personas.answer:
I was drawn to GeoAI because, after years of flying over flood‑prone territories, I saw the same gaps in every map – missing seasonal trails, unrecorded cultural sites, and outdated land cover that no satellite could capture without local input. The promise of machine learning to fuse high‑resolution imagery with Elders’ oral maps seemed a way to finally give our communities the situational awareness we’ve been forced to generate by hand.

What keeps me up at night is the prospect of those same algorithms being handed over to corporations or distant ministries without clear consent frameworks. When a model predicts a “optimal” evacuation route that cuts across a sacred burial ground, the error isn’t just technical; it erodes trust and can cause irreversible cultural loss. Without enforceable data‑sovereignty protocols built into every GeoAI pipeline, we risk turning our territories into open datasets for profit rather than tools for community safety.
